=== Republican era ===

==== Use until the 1960s, the 1965 restoration, and subsequent years ====

Following the [[Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey|proclamation of the Republic in Turkey]] in 1923, the tower continued to be used by the fire brigade and the [[Turkish Naval Forces]].{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=316}}<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Anadol"/>{{sfn|Koçu|1971|p=5907}} The [[time ball]] at the [[British Naval Hospital]], dismantled in February 1930 and installed atop the tower in March 1930, began operating in November 1934.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hem nalına hem mıhına |newspaper=[[Cumhuriyet]] |date=21 February 1930 |page=3 |first=Abidin |last=Daver |author-link=Abidin Daver}}</ref><ref name="küre">{{cite news |title=Saat ayarları birleşiyor |newspaper=Cumhuriyet |date=10 March 1930 |page=1}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Vakit küresi |newspaper=Cumhuriyet |date=8 November 1933 |page=2}}</ref>

During the winter of 1959–1960, the wooden rooms in the upper section were evacuated after their beams rotted and collapsed. Following an initiative by Istanbul Mayor [[Haşim İşcan]], it was decided to repair and restore the tower and convert it into a tourist facility.<ref name="Anadol"/> [[Yapı Merkezi|Yapıtaş]] won the tender for the work on 15 September 1964.<ref name="Anadol"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Galata Kulesi için proje hazırlandı |newspaper=[[Milliyet]] |date=5 September 1964 |page=2}}</ref><ref name="tesis">{{cite news |title=Galata Kulesi turistik tesis oluyor |newspaper=Milliyet |first=Orhan |last=Peksayar |date=21 September 1964 |pages=1, 7}}</ref> The tower reopened at a ceremony on 28 September 1967.{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=316}}<ref name="Anadol"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Galata Kulesine giriş 3 lira |newspaper=Milliyet |date=29 September 1967 |page=1}}</ref>

As part of the work, the [[basement]] was arranged as a service floor.<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Anadol-2">{{journal citation |url=http://dergi.mo.org.tr/dergiler/2/144/1718.pdf |title=Galata Kulesi'nin turistik tanzimi - II |first=Köksal |last=Anadol |journal=Arkitekt |year=1965 |volume=4 |issue=318 |pages=18-24|access-date=23 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101043420/http://dergi.mo.org.tr/dergiler/2/144/1718.pdf |archive-date=1 November 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> The ground floor became an entrance level, and two elevators running from this floor to the sixth floor were installed opposite the entrance axis.<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Bayrak">{{cite book |title=Türkiye Tarihi Yerler Kılavuzu |first=M. Orhan |last=Bayrak |page=295 |year=1979 |publisher=[[Remzi Kitabevi]]}}</ref> The first floor was arranged as an [[Ottoman coffeehouse|Oriental coffeehouse]], the second as a museum about the tower's history, the third as a sales floor for tourist souvenirs, the fourth as a tavern named Ceneviz Meyhanesi, the fifth as a kitchen for the tower's food and beverage facilities, the sixth as a lobby with [[toilet]]s and a [[cloakroom]], and the eighth floor—the highest floor accessible to visitors—as a [[nightclub]].<ref name="Anadol-3"/> Ünal Kardeşler, who built the restaurant section, also leased the tower's operating rights from the Istanbul Municipality for five years following a tender in February 1968.{{sfn|Koçu|1971|pp=1509-1510}} After the alterations, the tower officially opened as a tourist facility on 30 May 1969.<ref>{{cite news |title=Restore edilen tarihî Galata Kulesi açıldı |date=30 May 1969 |newspaper=Cumhuriyet |page=1}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Galata Kulesi yarından itibaren halka açılıyor |newspaper=Milliyet |date=29 May 1969 |page=11}}</ref> The brothers' lease agreement with the Municipality was renewed annually after the initial five-year period.<ref name="röportaj">{{cite news |title=Ayda 2.5 milyara kule |work=[[Hürriyet|Hürriyet İstanbul]] |date=8 June 2000 |first=Şengün |last=Kılıç |page=6}}</ref>

Under a Council of Ministers decision published in the ''T.C. Resmî Gazete'' on 3 September 1989 and brought into force, an area called Galata Tower and Its Surroundings was designated a "tourism center," bringing the tower and its surroundings under the authority of the [[Ministry of Culture and Tourism of Turkey]].<ref>{{cite gazette |url=https://www.resmigazete.gov.tr/arsiv/20281.pdf |title=Karar Sayısı : 89/14499 |pages=13-43 |date=13 September 1989 |issue=20281 |newspaper=[[T.C. Resmî Gazete]] |access-date=28 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190214220453/http://www.resmigazete.gov.tr/arsiv/20281.pdf |archive-date=14 February 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Radikal">{{cite web |url=http://www.radikal.com.tr/turkiye/mahkemeden-tarihi-karar-beyoglunu-turistlestiren-imar-plani-iptal-1167831/ |title=Mahkemeden tarihi karar: Beyoğlu'nu 'turistleştiren' imar planı iptal! |first=Elif |last=İnce |work=[[Radikal]] |date=24 December 2013 |location=Istanbul |access-date=31 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090818/http://www.radikal.com.tr/turkiye/mahkemeden-tarihi-karar-beyoglunu-turistlestiren-imar-plani-iptal-1167831/ |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== The 1999–2000 restoration and transfer to the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality ====

[[File:Galata Tower inside.jpg|thumb|A view from the tower's eighth floor, which housed a restaurant until 2020 (June 2011)]]

At a meeting of the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipal Council in October 1996, a decision was made to convert the tower into a museum and transfer its ownership to the Municipality's Directorate of Libraries and Museums.<ref>{{cite news |title=2 tartışmalı karar |newspaper=Milliyet |first=Arife |last=Avcu |location=Istanbul |date=5 October 1996 |page=3}}</ref> Pekerler İnşaat won the tender issued that year to restore the tower and convert it into a museum.<ref name="yenilendi">{{cite web |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/galata-kulesinin-disi-yenilendi-39184690 |title=Galata Kulesi'nin dışı yenilendi |work=Hürriyet |date=26 September 2000 |access-date=28 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090817/https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/galata-kulesinin-disi-yenilendi-39184690 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="kurtarılıyor">{{cite web |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/galata-kulesi-kurtariliyor-39081330 |title=Galata Kulesi kurtarılıyor |work=Hürriyet |date=24 September 1999 |access-date=28 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090818/https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/galata-kulesi-kurtariliyor-39081330 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref> A lawsuit filed that year to evict the Ünal Kardeşler company, which continued to operate the tower, was dismissed.<ref>{{cite news |title=Galata Kulesi müze haline getirilecek |first=Duygu |last=Durgun |newspaper=Cumhuriyet |date=15 October 1996 |page=20}}</ref><ref name="engel">{{cite news |title=Galata Kulesi'nde belediyeye engel |newspaper=Milliyet |date=14 December 1997 |page=7 |first=Arife |last=Avcu |location=Istanbul}}</ref> In December 1997, however, an order was issued to halt the project because such a change could not be made without the Ministry of Culture's permission, and the proposed museum use was deemed unsuitable.<ref name="engel"/> Although the Municipality attempted to establish a library in the tower in 1998, the proposal was rejected by the Conservation Board for Immovable Cultural and Natural Assets.<ref name="röportaj"/><ref name="savunma">{{cite news |title=Söz savunmanın |newspaper=Milliyet |date=12 June 2000 |page=6 |first=Mehmet |last=Demirkaya}}</ref>

Following an authorization decision issued by the Istanbul No. 1 Conservation Board for Cultural and Natural Assets on 7 May 1999, restoration of the exterior was completed by Peker İnşaat, which had won the 1996 tender, in June 2000. The tower reopened on 13 November 2000.<ref name="röportaj"/><ref name="kurtarılıyor"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/kelebek/galata-kulesi-genclesiyor-39180201 |title=Galata Kulesi gençleşiyor |work=Hürriyet Kelebek |date=6 September 2000 |access-date=28 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090818/https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/kelebek/galata-kulesi-genclesiyor-39180201 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/galatada-gurtuna-sovu-39198511 |title=Galata'da Gürtuna şovu |date=15 November 2000 |work=Hürriyet |access-date=4 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090826/https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/galatada-gurtuna-sovu-39198511 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref> Pekerler İnşaat also won the tender issued by the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality in 2000 for the interior restoration.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/galata-kulesi-restorasyonu-anitlar-kurulu-na-takildi-167899 |title=Galata Kulesi restorasyonu Anıtlar Kurulu'na takıldı |work=Hürriyet |date=28 August 2003 |first=Şenol |last=Çoşkuner |location=Istanbul |access-date=28 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090836/https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/galata-kulesi-restorasyonu-anitlar-kurulu-na-takildi-167899 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="izin">{{cite web |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/ic-restorasyon-izin-bekliyor-39203772 |title=İç restorasyon izin bekliyor |work=Hürriyet |date=4 December 2000 |access-date=4 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090925/https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/ic-restorasyon-izin-bekliyor-39203772 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, the Municipality's proposed interior restoration project, which envisaged converting the tower into a museum, was rejected by the Board because the Ministry of Culture, which was responsible for granting permission to establish a museum, had not issued the necessary authorization.<ref name="izin"/> Later that year, a new project featuring an exhibition hall, a souvenir shop, and a café was prepared and submitted to the Board.<ref name="izin"/> In February 2004, the Board approved a proposal to arrange the top two floors as a Turkish coffeehouse and the remaining floors for souvenir shops and other tourist facilities.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://v3.arkitera.com/v1/haberler/2003/09/27/galata.htm |title=Galata Kulesi restorasyonu Anıtlar'ı bekliyor |work=[[Zaman (newspaper)|Zaman]] |date=27 September 2003 |access-date=28 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004053557/http://v3.arkitera.com/v1/haberler/2003/09/27/galata.htm |archive-date=4 October 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.turkiyegazetesi.com.tr/Genel/a195471.aspx?/Genel/a195471.aspx& |title=Galata Kulesi nihayet |date=20 February 2004 |work=[[Türkiye (newspaper)|Türkiye]] |location=Istanbul |access-date=6 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090847/https://www.turkiyegazetesi.com.tr/Genel/a195471.aspx?%2FGenel%2Fa195471.aspx& |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Galata Tower - panoramio (5).jpg|thumb|left|A view of the restaurant on the tower's eighth floor before 2020, during the period when it was operated by [[BELTUR]] (April 2015)]]

Under a Council of Ministers decision published in the ''T.C. Resmî Gazete'' on 28 March 2006, Galata Tower and Its Surroundings was designated a "renewal area."<ref>{{cite gazette |url=https://www.resmigazete.gov.tr/eskiler/2006/03/20060328-5.htm |title=Bakanlar Kurulu kararı |issue=26122 |newspaper=T.C. Resmî Gazete |date=28 March 2006 |access-date=31 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161106044204/http://www.resmigazete.gov.tr/eskiler/2006/03/20060328-5.htm |archive-date=6 November 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Dinçer">{{cite journal |url=http://www.mimarlikdergisi.com/index.cfm?sayfa=mimarlik&DergiSayi=366&RecID=2323 |title=Kentsel Yenileme ve Dönüşüm: Deneyimler |first=İclal |last=Dinçer |year=2010 |journal=Mimarlık |pages=24-27|access-date=31 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090939/http://www.mimarlikdergisi.com/index.cfm?sayfa=mimarlik&DergiSayi=366&RecID=2323 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref> A further Council of Ministers decision published in the ''T.C. Resmî Gazete'' on 6 July 2006 stipulated that the Beyoğlu Municipality would expropriate the area as part of the renewal-area project.<ref name="Dinçer"/><ref>{{cite gazette |url=https://www.resmigazete.gov.tr/eskiler/2006/07/20060706-2.htm |title=Bakanlar Kurulu kararı |issue=26220 |newspaper=T.C. Resmî Gazete |date=6 July 2006 |access-date=31 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161106044033/http://www.resmigazete.gov.tr/eskiler/2006/07/20060706-2.htm |archive-date=6 November 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref> Although the area lay within parts of Beyoğlu designated an urban conservation area by a decision of the Istanbul No. 1 Conservation Board for Cultural and Natural Assets dated 7 July 1993, it was one of seven areas outside the planning area.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Mekânsal planların yargı denetimi ve karşılaşılan zorluklar, Beyoğlu (İstanbul) örneği |first=Adem Erdem |last=Erbaş |volume=5 |issue=2 |year=2020 |pages=103-118|journal=Journal of Awareness |doi=10.26809/joa.5.009 |issn=2149-6544 }}</ref>

Legal efforts to evict the tower's operators, ongoing since 1996, came to an end after the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality declined to renew the lease with the Kardeşler family, who operated the tower. On 16 April 2013, operation of the tower was transferred to BELTUR, a company affiliated with the Municipality.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/sobadan-sizan-gazdan-dolayi-yasli-cift-hayatini-kaybetti-41726247 |title=Alkol kavgası Galata Kulesi'ni kararttı |work=Hürriyet |date=2 March 2002 |access-date=28 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210127231025/https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/sobadan-sizan-gazdan-dolayi-yasli-cift-hayatini-kaybetti-41726247 |archive-date=27 January 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Akşam-beltur">{{cite web |url=https://www.aksam.com.tr/yasam/galata-kulesini-artik-beltur-isletiyor/haber-273203 |title=Galata Kulesi'ni artık Beltur işletiyor |work=[[Akşam (1994 newspaper)|Akşam]] |date=2 January 2014 |first=Şenol |last=Demirci |access-date=30 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160416065515/http://www.aksam.com.tr/yasam/galata-kulesini-artik-beltur-isletiyor/haber-273203 |archive-date=16 April 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref> Following renovations to the top two floors carried out by the Municipality, the eighth floor became a restaurant and the seventh a café.<ref name="Akşam-beltur"/>

At the 37th session of the [[World Heritage Committee]], a decision adopted on 21 June 2013 included the Galata Tower among the architectural works in the series entitled "Trade Posts and Fortifications on Genoese Trade Routes from the Mediterranean to the Black Sea" on [[UNESCO]]'s [[World Heritage Sites in Turkey|Tentative World Heritage List for Turkey]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bianet.org/bianet/kultur/148868-unesco-listesine-dort-yeni-aday |title=UNESCO listesine dört yeni aday |publisher=[[Bianet]] |date=31 July 2013 |access-date=1 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140821211854/http://www.bianet.org/bianet/kultur/148868-unesco-listesine-dort-yeni-aday |archive-date=21 August 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== General Directorate of Foundations period and the 2020 restoration ====

[[File:Galata Tower Lighting.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|The tower's present-day nighttime illumination (February 2021)]]

In a letter dated 17 April 2019, the [[Directorate General of Foundations]], invoking Article 30 of the [[Foundations Law]], applied for ownership of the tower to be transferred to it on behalf of the Kule-i Zemin Foundation.<ref name="Güvemli">{{cite web |url=https://www.sozcu.com.tr/2020/gundem/galata-kulesine-ihtiyati-tedbir-konuldu-5646575/ |title=Galata Kulesi’ne ihtiyati tedbir konuldu |first=Özlem |last=Güvemli |work=Sözcü |date=26 February 2020 |access-date=31 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200227163851/https://www.sozcu.com.tr/2020/gundem/galata-kulesine-ihtiyati-tedbir-konuldu-5646575/ |archive-date=27 February 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Boğazlıyan">{{cite web |url=https://www.haberturk.com/ibb-den-alinip-vakiflar-a-devredilen-galata-kulesi-nin-arka-plani-2595195 |title=İBB'den alınıp Vakıflar'a devredilen Galata Kulesi'nin arka planı |first=Esra |last=Boğazlıyan |publisher=[[Haberturk.com]] |date=25 February 2020 |access-date=31 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201206115043/https://www.haberturk.com/ibb-den-alinip-vakiflar-a-devredilen-galata-kulesi-nin-arka-plani-2595195 |archive-date=6 December 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> As of 13 May 2019, ownership of the tower was transferred to the General Directorate of Foundations on behalf of the Kule-i Zemin Foundation, while the Municipality remained a tenant.<ref name="Boğazlıyan"/> Legal action initiated by the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality against the transfer was unsuccessful, and the lease agreement issued to BELTUR expired on 31 December 2019.<ref name="Güvemli"/><ref name="Boğazlıyan"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/haber/galata-kulesinde-bakan-belturu-sucladi-1739259 |title=Galata Kulesi'nde Bakan Beltur'u suçladı |work=Cumhuriyet |date=17 May 2020 |first=Selda |last=Güneysu |access-date=6 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090854/https://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/haber/galata-kulesinde-bakan-belturu-sucladi-1739259 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 18 January 2020, Minister of Culture and Tourism [[Mehmet Nuri Ersoy]] announced that expropriation work would be carried out around the tower and a public square would be created as part of the tourism, culture, and arts project known as the "Beyoğlu Culture Route," which included the Galata Tower.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/kultur-sanat/kultur-ve-turizm-bakani-ersoy-beyoglu-kultur-yolu-planini-acikladi/1706776 |title=Kültür ve Turizm Bakanı Ersoy Beyoğlu Kültür Yolu Planı'nı açıkladı |first1=Musa |last1=Alcan |first2=Hilal |last2=Uştuk |first3=Fatih |last3=Türkyılmaz |publisher=[[Anadolu Agency]] |date=18 January 2020 |location=Istanbul |access-date=31 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200119155216/https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/kultur-sanat/kultur-ve-turizm-bakani-ersoy-beyoglu-kultur-yolu-planini-acikladi/1706776 |archive-date=19 January 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> In April 2020, the process of evicting the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality from the tower began. The Municipality's legal challenge was unsuccessful, and as of 16 May 2020, ownership of the tower passed to the Istanbul Regional Directorate of Foundations No. 1 on behalf of the Kule-i Zemin Foundation.<ref name="Güvemli"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sozcu.com.tr/2020/gundem/galata-kulesini-ibbden-alma-girisimine-mahkeme-dur-dedi-5755484/ |title=Galata Kulesi'ni İBB'den alma girişimine mahkeme "dur" dedi |work=Sözcü |first=Özlem |last=Güvemli |date=17 April 2020 |access-date=1 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200429144235/https://www.sozcu.com.tr/2020/gundem/galata-kulesini-ibbden-alma-girisimine-mahkeme-dur-dedi-5755484/ |archive-date=29 April 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Karaaslan">{{cite web |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/turkiye/vakiflar-genel-muduru-ersoydan-galata-kulesinin-mulkiyet-hakkina-iliskin-degerlendirme/1842048 |title=Vakıflar Genel Müdürü Ersoy'dan Galata Kulesi'nin mülkiyet hakkına ilişkin değerlendirme |publisher=Anadolu Agency |date=15 May 2020 |first=Yeşim Sert |last=Karaaslan |access-date=1 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200613115854/https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/turkiye/vakiflar-genel-muduru-ersoydan-galata-kulesinin-mulkiyet-hakkina-iliskin-degerlendirme/1842048 |archive-date=13 June 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/haber/galata-kulesinde-neler-oluyor-ibb-suc-duyurusunda-bulunacak-1757904 |title=Galata Kulesi'nde neler oluyor? İBB suç duyurusunda bulunacak |work=Cumhuriyet |date=12 August 2020 |access-date=1 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200919114531/https://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/haber/galata-kulesinde-neler-oluyor-ibb-suc-duyurusunda-bulunacak-1757904 |archive-date=19 September 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref>

ES Yapı, which won the tender for the restoration work, began work on 30 June 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.vgm.gov.tr/haberler/galata-kulesi-bir-vakif-eserdir-tum-insanligin-mirasidir |title=Galata Kulesi bir vakıf eseridir, tüm insanlığın mirasıdır. |publisher=[[Directorate General of Foundations]] |date=15 August 2020 |access-date=1 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201124095925/https://www.vgm.gov.tr/haberler/galata-kulesi-bir-vakif-eserdir-tum-insanligin-mirasidir |archive-date=24 November 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> All elements and decorations added to the interior during the work of the 1960s and afterward were removed, and restoration and renovation work was carried out on both the interior and exterior.<ref name="Habertürk">{{cite web |url=https://www.haberturk.com/galata-kulesi-restorasyonu-tamamladi-2826573 |title=Ersoy: Bin ton betonu söktük, bin kamyonet yükü attık |publisher=Haberturk.com |date=7 October 2020 |first=Yavuz |last=Barlas |access-date=4 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030224932/https://www.haberturk.com/galata-kulesi-restorasyonu-tamamladi-2826573 |archive-date=30 October 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://aydinlik.com.tr/haber/hafifleyen-arinan-galata-artik-sadece-muze-220163 |title=Hafifleyen, arınan Galata artık sadece müze |work=[[Aydınlık]] |date=7 October 2020 |access-date=5 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201107001454/https://aydinlik.com.tr/haber/hafifleyen-arinan-galata-artik-sadece-muze-220163 |archive-date=7 November 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> The tower was redesigned as an exhibition center and museum and reopened on 6 October 2020, the anniversary of the [[Liberation of Istanbul]], under the name Galata Tower Museum.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/kultur-sanat/istanbulun-simgelerinden-galata-kulesi-ziyarete-acildi/1997972 |title=İstanbul'un simgelerinden galata kulesi ziyarete açıldı |publisher=Anadolu Agency |first=Aişe Hümeyra |last=Bulovalı |date=6 October 2020 |access-date=2 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090859/https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/kultur-sanat/istanbulun-simgelerinden-galata-kulesi-ziyarete-acildi/1997972 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref>

As part of the work, a ticket booth designed to resemble the nostalgic Taksim–Tünel tramcars of the [[T2 (Istanbul Tram)|Taksim–Tünel tram line]] was installed in the square outside the tower.<ref name="Duvar">{{cite web |url=https://www.gazeteduvar.com.tr/galata-kulesinin-bugununu-tasarlamak-makale-1503564 |title=Galata Kulesi'nin bugününü tasarlamak |first=Hakkı |last=Yırtıcı |work=[[Gazete Duvar]] |date=5 November 2020 |access-date=2 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201104230729/https://www.gazeteduvar.com.tr/galata-kulesinin-bugununu-tasarlamak-makale-1503564 |archive-date=4 November 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> The ground floor was arranged as a ticket-control and security area, with the entrance to the elevator reaching the sixth floor also located there.<ref name="Duvar"/><ref name="AA">{{cite web |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/kultur-sanat/galata-kulesi-yeniden-ziyaretcilerini-agirlamaya-basladi/1998928 |title=Galata Kulesi yeniden ziyaretçilerini ağırlamaya başladı |publisher=Anadolu Agency |first=Ahmet Esad |last=Şani |date=7 October 2020 |access-date=2 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090901/https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/kultur-sanat/galata-kulesi-yeniden-ziyaretcilerini-agirlamaya-basladi/1998928 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref> The first floor became a museum shop.<ref name="Duvar"/> The second floor was arranged as a simulation area featuring a screen showing an animation of [[Hezârfen Ahmed Çelebi]] gliding from the Galata Tower, as well as an exhibition area covering the period when the tower was used as an observatory.<ref name="Duvar"/><ref name="AA"/> The third floor was renovated as a permanent exhibition space for photographs from the [[Turkish War of Independence]], the fourth for information and artifacts relating to the Galata Tower and its walls, and the fifth for exhibits concerning the Galata Tower and Istanbul.<ref name="Duvar"/> On the seventh floor, reached after the sixth-floor transitional area, a temporary exhibition space was created with a scale model depicting part of Istanbul and viewing telescopes positioned by the windows.<ref name="Duvar"/> The eighth floor was arranged as an observation terrace.<ref name="Duvar"/>

Restoration work on the tower's roof began on 1 November 2023, carried out by Galata Restorasyon.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ihaleciler.com/ihale/1680729373822.htm |title=Eski Eser Binalarının Kısmi Restorasyonu ve Muhtelif Yapım Onarım İşi |publisher=İhaleciler.com |access-date=14 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231114214805/https://www.ihaleciler.com/ihale/1680729373822.htm |archive-date=14 November 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/istanbul-valiligi-duyurdu-galata-kulesinde-restorasyon-basladi-42355217 |title=İstanbul Valiliği duyurdu: Galata Kulesi'nde restorasyon başladı |work=Hürriyet |date=2 November 2023 |access-date=14 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231114234751/https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/istanbul-valiligi-duyurdu-galata-kulesinde-restorasyon-basladi-42355217 |archive-date=14 November 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ntv.com.tr/galeri/n-life/kultur-ve-sanat/galata-kulesinin-kulahi-restore-ediliyor,2zd75FuNYkaH_Ya8ylZfig/n5eDx7gBf0SjPDnCUYzV2w |title=Galata Kulesi'nin külahı restore ediliyor |publisher=[[NTV (Turkish TV channel)|NTV.com.tr]] |agency=[[İhlas News Agency]] |date=7 November 2023 |access-date=14 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231114214756/https://www.ntv.com.tr/galeri/n-life/kultur-ve-sanat/galata-kulesinin-kulahi-restore-ediliyor,2zd75FuNYkaH_Ya8ylZfig/n5eDx7gBf0SjPDnCUYzV2w |archive-date=14 November 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Location and architecture ==
=== Location, exterior architecture, and structure ===
{{multiple image|
| align             = right
| direction         = vertical
| image1            = Istanbul asv2020-02 img46 Galata Bridge and Tower.jpg
| image2            = Galata, Beyoğlu - Aerial view - 01.jpg
| footer            = Views of the tower and its surroundings from the [[Golden Horn]] (top, February 2020) and from the air (July 2011)
}}
The Galata Tower is building number 2 on Büyük Hendek Street, located in the Bereketzade neighbourhood of the [[Beyoğlu]] district of [[Istanbul]].<ref name="KTB"/> It stands in the Galata neighbourhood, which gave it its name, on a hill at an elevation of 35 m.{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=314}} The tower is a cylindrical masonry structure in the [[Romanesque architecture|Romanesque]] style,<ref name="Anadol"/><ref>{{cite journal |url=https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/508818 |title=Taş ve taş yapı kültüründe değişim ve dönüşüm |first=İkbal |last=Erbaş |journal=ATA Planlama ve Tasarım Dergisi |volume=2 |issue=1 |year=2018 |pages=29–37|publisher=[[Atatürk University]] Faculty of Architecture and Design |access-date=25 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200326004415/https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/508818 |archive-date=26 March 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> with a height of 62.59 m from ground level to the tip of its roof.<ref name="Anadol-3"/> Situated on rocky, clay-rich schist ground, the building has a solid stone foundation.{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=316}} The entrance door, located above ground level on the southern axis, is reached by marble staircases on either side.<ref name="Anadol"/> Above the tower's marble entrance door, which has jambs in the Empire style, is an inscription commemorating the repair and restoration works carried out in 1831–1832. The inscription bears a poem by [[Ethem Pertev Pasha|Poet Pertev]].<ref name="Anadol"/>{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=315}} The text, carved into the marble in relief by Nuri Dede and written in the jali style of [[Taliq script|ta'liq calligraphy]], consists of 16 verses arranged in four lines across four panels, framed by cartouches with serrated borders. Three elliptical cartouches above the text read, respectively, "Ya Hafiz", "Maşallah", and "Ya Rafi".{{sfn|Arpacı|2020|pp=566–569}} The [[tughra]] of Mahmud II, which had previously appeared on the inscription, was chiselled away after the [[Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey|proclamation of the republic]].{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=315}} On the southern-facing facade, at ground-floor level, a plaque prepared by [[Emin Barın]] was installed in 1953, following an initiative by the [[Istanbul Conquest Society]], to mark the 500th anniversary of the [[Fall of Constantinople]]. The plaque bears the following text in capital letters:{{sfn|Arpacı|2020|p=40}}<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.istanbulfetihcemiyeti.org.tr/hakkimizda_k1.html|title=İstanbul Fetih Cemiyeti Hakkında|publisher=[[Istanbul Conquest Society]]|access-date=26 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200601175927/http://www.istanbulfetihcemiyeti.org.tr/hakkimizda_k1.html|archive-date=1 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=La Repubblica di Genova tra nobili e popolari: 1257-1528 |first=Giuseppe |last=Gallo |publisher=De Ferrari |year=1997 |page=75 |language=Italian |isbn=887172092X}}</ref>

{{quote|On the morning of Tuesday, 29 May 1453, the Genoese colony of Galata presented its keys to Fatih Sultan Mehmed, and the surrender of Galata was completed on Friday, 1 June.<br>Istanbul Conquest Society. 1953<br>EB{{efn|The initials of Emin Barın, who prepared the text, forming his signature.{{sfn|Arpacı|2020|p=40}}}}}}

In the square outside the tower is a ticket booth designed in the style of the [[T2 (Istanbul Tram)|Taksim–Tünel nostalgic tram]].<ref name="Duvar"/> Adjacent to the surviving sections of the walls surrounding the tower, with its front facing the tower square, stands the Bereketzade Fountain, which was dismantled from its former location and moved here in 1957.<ref name="Sağlam"/>{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=316}}

The ground floor has an area of 208 m², an internal diameter of 8.95 m, and an external diameter of 16.45 m. The wall thickness, which is 3.75 m up to the fourth floor, decreases to 3 m from that floor upward because the tower was built with an outward slope.<ref name="Sağlam"/><ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Anadol"/> Although a 5 m section of the external walls at entrance-door level loses its circular shape, this irregularity diminishes up to the first cornice, after which the building resumes its circular form. At a height of 4.2 m, on the entrance axis, there is a channel opening measuring 72 × 150 cm, topped by a brick vault. Anadol suggests that these channels may once have extended outside the tower and continued beneath the walls, providing connections between the fortifications.<ref name="Anadol"/>

[[File:Galata Tower January 2015.JPG|thumb|left|upright=0.7|A photograph of the tower showing the surrounding walls and the brick bands on its exterior (January 2015)]] The interior architecture of the tower and the materials used in its walls remain consistent up to the fourth floor. Irregular [[embrasure]]s in the floor plans and the flattened profile of the southern facade continue uninterrupted from the ground floor to the fourth floor. Above this level, the embrasures become regular and the shaft assumes a fully cylindrical shape. Two horizontal brick bands run around the tower's shaft, at elevations of 13.20 m (the beginning of the second floor) and 17.17 m (the beginning of the third floor). The section below the first band consists of roughly dressed, square-shaped stone blocks of various types, in irregular arrangements and in dark yellow, light brown, dark grey, and dark blue hues, with fragments of brick inserted between them. Above this band, the stones are comparatively smaller, more finely dressed, generally horizontally rectangular, and arranged more regularly; there are no brick fragments between the stones. Limestone is the most commonly used stone in this section. Yellow and brown tones are almost entirely absent, while dark grey and bluish colours remain prevalent.

Based on these observations, Sağlam states that "it is not possible to say that either the first band or the second band alone represents the level separating the Genoese and Ottoman periods". He argues that the collapse caused by the 1509 earthquake was not level, as "previous researchers had assumed", but irregular, with the inner section reaching a higher level. Based on the change in stonework above the first band, he concludes that damage and material loss to the exterior extended as far as the second floor, while the thick-walled section of the shaft and its internal vaulted gallery were preserved "to a large extent" up to the fourth floor. Damage to the exterior from the second floor upward was also repaired. From the fourth floor onward, the entire level was flattened, marking the beginning of a new section with thinner walls and a different staircase system. He further suggests that the brick bands served as hatıl (bonding courses), helping distribute weight evenly between the repaired sections and the original shaft walls.<ref name="Sağlam"/>

On the southern-facing section of the second brick band is an Ottoman-style decorative motif made of bricks. Diagonal cracks at the joints in this section have created a distinct pattern. According to Sağlam, this indicates that "the section assumed to date from the Genoese period actually contains at least two phases, rather than just one".<ref name="Sağlam"/>

The top of the tower is covered by a conical, lead-clad reinforced-concrete roof.{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=316}}<ref name="Anadol-3"/> The roof has four windows, each facing one of the cardinal directions, with their upper limits reaching an elevation of 50.29 m.<ref name="Anadol-3"/> At the summit is a gold-plated bronze finial, measuring 7.41 m according to Anadol and 6.75 m according to Şevket Usta, who manufactured it.<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="alem">{{cite news |title=Şevket Usta'nın yaptığı altın kaplama alem İstanbul'un üstüne yerleşti |newspaper=Hürriyet |date=17 April 1967 |page=10 |first=Metin |last=Soysal}}</ref> A 50 cm lantern is installed at the top of the finial. It has a flashing red light that makes the tower visible and also serves as a lightning rod.<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="alem"/>

=== Interior architecture ===
[[File:Interior stairs of the Galata Tower.jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|A view of the tower's staircase (June 2021)]]
The building has eleven floors in total, including a [[basement]], a ground floor, and a [[mezzanine]]. The first four floors are connected by a gallery passage with stone stairs protected by wood coated in [[epoxy]]. The stairs are set directly into the shaft walls, and the passage is covered by brick vaults.<ref name="Sağlam"/><ref>{{cite mailing list |url=https://prnt.sc/y6oafw |title=Vakıflar Genel Müdürlüğünden yapılan bilgilendirme |last=Kazık |first=Ali Efe |institution=General Directorate of Foundations |date=2 February 2021 |access-date=3 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207213240/https://prnt.sc/y6oafw |archive-date=7 February 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref> During excavation work carried out as part of the restoration in the 1960s, no floor surface was found down to an elevation of −4.3 m. The area was excavated to reinforce the foundations, creating a basement at −3.8 m. From here, a reinforced-concrete staircase concealed beneath a circular floor panel leads to the ground floor.<ref name="Anadol-3"/> The staircase connecting the ground floor to the upper floors has 22 steps and is located 42 cm from the tower's inner wall. It is 80 cm wide and 150 cm high.<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Bayrak"/> On the entrance floor, whose ceiling is covered with hexagonal natural stone, two lifts, each accommodating eight people, are positioned opposite the entrance door along its axis, against the wall. They extend to the sixth floor.<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Bayrak"/><ref name="AA"/> The lifts use video-wall technology to display footage filmed from the tower on screens installed on their walls and ceilings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.haberasansoru.com.tr/istanbulun-gozdesi-galata-kulesine-yerli-asansor/|title=İstanbul'un gözdesi Galata Kulesi'ne yerli asansör|work=Haber Asansörü|first=Yeliz|last=Karakütük|date=4 January 2021|access-date=3 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210106080037/http://www.haberasansoru.com.tr/istanbulun-gozdesi-galata-kulesine-yerli-asansor/|archive-date=6 January 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> Above the reinforced-concrete mezzanine, which stands at an elevation of 4.45 m and has balustrades with Empire-style profiles, is the first floor, at 8.97 m. The first-floor window openings measure 20 × 45 cm on the exterior and 200 × 180 cm on the interior.<ref name="Anadol"/> The second floor, at 13.20 m, shares the same architectural characteristics as the first floor, except that its internal diameter decreases to 8.85 m.<ref name="Anadol"/>

[[File:Galata Tower-renovated elevators (5th floor).jpg|thumb|left|A view from the fifth floor (January 2021)]] Within the niches in the third-floor walls, at an elevation of 17.17 m, are chimneys that Anadol considered "similar" to those of Zağanos Pasha Tower at [[Rumeli Fortress]]. The fourth floor, at 20.80 m, contains 14 rectangular windows. Because the brickwork gallery reduces the thickness of the shaft wall, it is positioned only on the southern side, the safer direction facing the colonial settlement. This arrangement ensures that the wall remains at its full thickness on the side most exposed to potential attacks from outside. As a result of this reduction in wall thickness, the internal diameter increases to 10.4 m. The average dimensions of the bricks used in the vaulted galleries of the first four floors resemble those of bricks found in other fourteenth-century fortifications in Galata and in late Byzantine structures elsewhere in the city. Sağlam considers the use of locally sourced materials in the tower's construction "a reasonable possibility". At this floor, the number of windows increases to seven.<ref name="Sağlam"/><ref name="Anadol"/><ref name="KTB">{{cite web|url=https://istanbul.ktb.gov.tr/TR-165615/galata-kulesi.html|title=Galata Kulesi|publisher=[[Ministry of Culture and Tourism (Turkey)|Republic of Turkey Ministry of Culture and Tourism]], Istanbul Provincial Directorate of Culture and Tourism|access-date=25 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108172034/https://istanbul.ktb.gov.tr/TR-165615/galata-kulesi.html|archive-date=8 January 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Galata Tower-seventh floor.jpg|thumb|A view from the seventh floor (January 2021)]] The fifth floor begins at an elevation of 24.35 m and has 14 windows. Seven of these, installed for firing [[cannon]]s, are circular and 35 cm in diameter; the other seven measure 115 × 180 cm and have [[pointed arch]]es. All the windows on this floor are set into niches within masonry piers whose arches are constructed of brick. The sixth floor, at 27.90 m, is the last of the wooden half-storeys. It has 14 pointed-arch windows similar to those on the floor below, but smaller. Above this is the seventh-floor lookout pavilion, beginning at an elevation of 32.60 m. The sixth, seventh, and eighth floors are connected by steel staircases. The 14 windows on the seventh floor are formed by 13 masonry piers, each measuring 120 × 225 cm in cross-section, spaced 150 cm apart and connected by arches. The eighth floor, at an elevation of 40.04 m, has an internal width of 12.40 m and extends up to an elevation of 50.5 m. Its 14 windows are formed by piers measuring 110 × 100 cm in cross-section, spaced 170 cm apart and connected by arches. These piers are aligned with those on the seventh floor. Outside the eighth floor is a terrace 1.20 m wide, created by the difference in cross-section between the two floors. Each of the 14 masonry posts positioned along the axes of the interior piers supports a stone sphere 35 cm in diameter, secured with anchors as a precaution against falling. The 110 cm-high iron railings between the posts feature Empire-style ornamentation.<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Anadol"/><ref name="KTB"/>{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=314}}<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=Galata Kulesi |encyclopedia=[[Dünden Bugüne İstanbul Ansiklopedisi]] |page=361 |first=Semavi |last=Eyice |volume=3 |publisher=[[Ministry of Culture and Tourism (Turkey)|Republic of Turkey Ministry of Culture]]–[[History Foundation]] |year=1994 |isbn=9757306037}}</ref>

Following the 2020 restoration, the interior walls and ceilings were coated with plaster.<ref name="Duvar"/> Exhibits related to the tower are displayed on the second floor, which serves as a museum shop, and on the third, fourth, fifth, and seventh floors, which serve as exhibition spaces and a museum. On the seventh floor, there is a 1:2,500-scale model depicting part of Istanbul, along with viewing telescopes positioned in front of the windows.<ref name="Duvar"/><ref name="AA"/> Benches are provided on the eighth floor, which is used as an observation terrace.<ref name="Duvar"/>

=== Architectural differences in earlier periods ===
==== 1348–1509 ====
{{multiple image
|align=right
|direction=horizontal
|image1=The Galata Tower in Liber insularum Archipelagi (1420s-1430s).jpg
|width1=64
|image2=The Galata Tower in Liber insularum Archipelagi, Düsseldorf copy.png
|width2=120
|footer=Depictions in copies of ''Liber insularum Archipelagi'' held by the ''[[Biblioteca Marciana]]'' (left, 1420s–1430s) and the [[University and State Library Düsseldorf]] (1485–1490), considered the closest representations of the tower during the Genoese period}}
When construction was completed, the tower served as the principal tower of the [[Galata Walls]], of which it formed a part. In front of the tower was a [[barbican]] that projected in a semicircle from the straight line of the walls and adjoined the tower on both sides. Because the outer side of the walls was surrounded by a [[moat]], the space between the tower and the barbican formed a courtyard. Some remains of this structure survive today. During the Genoese period, a [[cross]] stood atop the tower. Traces also indicate that the tower had a wooden bridge, now lost, that could be removed when necessary and provided passage between the city and the area outside the moats.<ref name="Sağlam"/>{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=316}}

In the various surviving versions of Cristoforo Buondelmonti's ''Liber insularum Archipelagi'', now held in different archives, the tower is depicted in several different ways, with inconsistencies among the illustrations. The cylindrical depictions are considered the closest to the original. On a map of Constantinople in the copy held by the ''[[Biblioteca Marciana]]'', dated to around the 1420s–1430s, the tower is shown as taller than the other towers, with a conical roof, a cylindrical body, and an upper storey projecting outward beneath a series of [[blind arch]]es. In a map in the copy of the same work dated to 1485–1490 and held by the [[University and State Library Düsseldorf]], a Genoese flag appears at the top of the tower. Comparing the two depictions, Sağlam notes that in the first, the tower's "narrow and relatively tall" conical roof is surrounded by a [[battlement]]ed parapet, whereas in the second, the roof is "much flatter and wider", with its eaves extending beyond the battlements. Sağlam also points out that the second copy shows "a single band dividing the tower's body wall horizontally right through the middle, as if marking a repair", suggesting, as a hypothesis, that this may corroborate the damage and repairs carried out in 1453.<ref name="Sağlam"/>

Following the Ottoman conquest of the area in 1453, the tower suffered damage that, according to anonymous Ottoman sources cited by [[Ahmed Vefik Pasha]], reduced its height by approximately 7.5 m. After an imperial decree concerning Pera was issued, the destruction was halted, the tower was raised again, and the cross at its summit was replaced with an [[Ottoman flag]].<ref name="Sağlam"/>

{{multiple image |align=center |total_width=500 |footer=Some depictions of the tower from its early period in various copies of Cristoforo Buondelmonti's ''Liber insularum Archipelagi'' (from left to right): the copy held by the [[National Maritime Museum]] and dated to the 1420s; the copy held by the [[Vatican Library]] and dated to 1465; the copy held by the [[National Library of France]] and dated to 1465–1475; the copy held by the [[National Central Library of Florence]] and dated to around 1470; the copy held by the [[Walters Art Museum]] and dated to around 1475; the copy held by the [[Bodleian Library]] and dated to the fifteenth century; and the version in [[Henricus Martellus Germanus]]'s ''Insularium Illustratum'', dated to 1495. |image1=The Galata Tower in Liber insularum Archipelagi, RMG copy.tiff |image2=Galata Tower in Liber Insularum Archipelagi (Vatican Library).png |image3=The Galata Tower (Buondelmonti, BNF).jpg |image4=The Galata Tower in Liber insularum Archipelagi (Florence copy).jpg |image5=The Galata Tower in the map of Constantinople in Liber insularum Archipelagi (Walters Art Museum).jpg |image6=The Galata Tower in Liber insularum Archipelagi (Bodleian copy).png |image7=Galata Tower (Insularium Illustratum).jpeg }}

==== 1509–1794 ====
Following the [[1509 Constantinople earthquake]], the tower sustained damage. Repairs were completed in mid-1510, and the tower was raised again.<ref name="Sağlam"/>{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=314}} The two brick bands around the tower's shaft, at elevations of 13.20 m (the beginning of the second floor) and 17.17 m (the beginning of the third floor), are considered evidence of alterations made after the earthquake. Köksal Anadol and Ersin Arıoğlu state that these bands indicate that the tower was rebuilt from these levels upward.<ref name="Anadol-3"/> [[Semavi Eyice]], on the other hand, notes that the brick motifs have "the typical character of Ottoman ornamentation". He argues that the relatively "plain" first band indicates a superficial repair to the exterior of the tower, while the section above the second band was built entirely during the Ottoman period.{{sfn|Eyice|1969|pp=25, 36–37, 63, 75}} In a miniature depicting the Galata Tower in a work by [[Matrakçı Nasuh]] dated to 1537, the lookout pavilion and the storey above it are shown in a 1:2 proportion, with approximately eight [[arch]]ed openings on the pavilion floor.<ref name="Anadol"/><ref>{{cite journal |url=https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/401659 |title=Matrakçı Nasuh'un Galata ve İstanbul minyatürlerinin harita tekniği açısından incelenmesi |first=Hüseyin Zayit |last=Selvi |first2=Gaye |last2=Bekiroğlu Keskin |journal=İSTEM |issue=29 |year=2017 |pages=25–39|access-date=19 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090900/https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/401659 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref>

{{multiple image |align=center |total_width=500 |footer=Some depictions of the tower from 1509 to 1794 (from left to right): a miniature in Matrakçı Nasuh's work published in 1537; a sixteenth-century engraving by Giovanni Andrea Vavassore; a miniature by Mustafa bin Mehmed Cündî in a 1629 copy of [[Piri Reis]]'s ''[[Kitab-ı Bahriye]]''; an engraving by Jaspar Isaac dated to 1650–1659; and an engraving by [[Paul Lucas (traveller)|Paul Lucas]] dated to 1720. |image1=Matrakçı Nasuh - The Galata Tower.jpg |image2=Houghton 51-2570 - Valvassori (cropped, the Galata Tower).jpg |image3=Galata Tower, 1629 (Kitab-ı Bahriye).jpg |image4=The Galata Tower from a Constantinople engraving by Jaspar Isaac.jpg |image5=Tour de Galatas - Lucas Paul - 1720.jpg }}

==== 1509–1965 ====
A fire on 27 July 1794 damaged the tower's roof and upper floors. The tower's height was reduced by approximately 1.9 m, and the walls in this section were rebuilt. As part of these works, an Empire-style pavilion with glazed projections approximately 1.5 m long was constructed on each side of the top floor.{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=315}}<ref name="Anadol"/>

Following the damage caused by a fire on 2–3 August 1831, repairs were carried out and the design of the tower's upper section was altered. The four projecting structures were replaced by a hall with 14 semicircular-arched windows in its walls. In front of the smaller-diameter, windowed storey above it, an iron-railed balcony was added around the building. A staircase with 40 steps in the centre of the hall provided access to the upper floor. The second floor, which contained the 14 windows, was covered by a conical lead roof with four windows installed above it.{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=315}}<ref name="Anadol"/>

After the roof was blown off during a storm in 1875, two octagonal timber-framed masonry storeys were built above the top floor, with a terrace at an elevation of 51.65 m. A flagpole was erected on top of these storeys. The spiral staircase connecting the two floors was removed and replaced with a straight wooden staircase inclined at 45 degrees to reach the upper floor.{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=316}}<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Anadol"/>{{sfn|Koçu|1971|p=5907}} In March 1930, a [[time ball]] was installed at the top of the tower.<ref name="küre"/>

==== 1965–2020 ====
[[File:20131205 Istanbul 311.jpg|thumb|A view from the terrace before the 2020 restoration (December 2013)]] During the restoration in 1965, the area around the tower was closed to traffic and reserved exclusively for pedestrians. It was also redesigned to accommodate several souvenir shops.<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Anadol-2"/> The stairs leading into the tower and the terrace in front of the entrance were enclosed by iron railings between marble posts.<ref name="Anadol-2"/><ref name="yarın">{{cite news |title=Galata Kulesi yarın açılıyor |newspaper=Milliyet |date=27 September 1967 |page=3}}</ref> The entrance door was renovated with detailing intended to be "close to the characteristics of the period".<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Anadol-2"/> The wooden floors were replaced with reinforced-concrete floors and were generally covered with natural stone. The stone stair treads were also clad in natural stone, and the staircases were illuminated.<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Anadol-2"/>

The wooden staircase in the centre of the seventh floor, which had been converted into a restaurant, was removed and replaced by steel staircases connecting the sixth, seventh, and eighth floors. These were fitted with wooden handrails and steps proportioned in the Empire style. The window frames and wall decorations on the floor were simplified to make more of the window glass visible. The tower's roof was rebuilt using a lead-clad reinforced-concrete system, retaining the conical design used between 1832 and 1876, although with a somewhat less pointed profile. A gold-plated bronze finial was installed on top. Cracks in the tower walls were repaired, and the load-bearing system was reinforced with reinforced-concrete elements.{{sfn|Eyice|1995|p=316}}<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="yarın"/><ref name="Mimdap">{{cite web|url=http://mimdap.org/2010/10/bir-landmarkyn-tarih-ycinde-dedhithimi/|title=Bir "landmark"ın tarih içinde değişimi|publisher=Mimdap.org|date=4 October 2010|access-date=27 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101031541/http://mimdap.org/2010/10/bir-landmarkyn-tarih-ycinde-dedhithimi/|archive-date=1 November 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> A relief depicting the miniature of Galata by Matrakçı Nasuh, created by [[Tankut Öktem]] and [[Haluk Tezonar]], was installed above the ground-floor entrance to the lift.<ref name="Anadol-3"/><ref name="Bayrak"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.birgun.net/haber/galata-kulesi-ndeki-alci-rolyefe-ne-oldu-313267|title=Galata Kulesi'ndeki alçı rölyefe ne oldu?|first=Uğur|last=Şahin|work=[[BirGün]]|date=25 August 2020|access-date=4 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201029042955/https://www.birgun.net/haber/galata-kulesi-ndeki-alci-rolyefe-ne-oldu-313267|archive-date=29 October 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Symbolic significance and events ==
{{multiple image
|align=right
|image1=Istanbul Oct 2019 12 26 09 765000.jpeg
|width1=160
|image2=Galata Tower 20191028 (cropped).jpg
|width2=170
|footer=The tower illuminated in pink to raise awareness of [[breast cancer]] (top, 19 October 2019) and with the [[Turkish flag]] projected onto it to celebrate [[Republic Day (Turkey)|Republic Day]] (28 October 2019)}}
The tower is one of the symbolic landmarks of Beyoğlu and Istanbul.<ref name="Mimdap"/><ref>{{cite journal |url=https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/mephoj/issue/58058/677155 |title=A Deep learning integrated mobile application for historic landmark recognition: A case study of Istanbul |first=Bülent |last=Bayram |first2=Batuhan |last2=Kılıç |first3=Furkan |last3=Özoğlu |first4=Fırat |last4=Erdem |first5=Tolga |last5=Bakirman |first6=Sinan |last6=Sivri |first7=Onur Can |last7=Bayrak |first8=Ahmet |last8=Delen |year=2020 |journal=Mersin Photogrammetry Journal |volume=2 |issue=2 |pages=38–50|language=English |access-date=24 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210524082334/https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/mephoj/issue/58058/677155 |archive-date=24 May 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref> It is also a tourist attraction, both because of its symbolic significance for the city and because its summit offers views over the city centre. Over time, restaurants, cafés, and shops have opened in its surroundings as a result of this popularity.<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/460813 |title=Bir yaratıcı küme örneği: Galata |first=Arbil |last=Öktünç |first2=Burcu |last2=Selcen Coşkun |journal=İdealkent |issue=7 |volume=3 |year=2012 |pages=84–109|issn=1307-9905 |access-date=18 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200326035702/https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/460813 |archive-date=26 March 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The tower is periodically illuminated in different colours on days commemorating events, raising awareness, or celebrating particular occasions. Images are also projected onto its shaft using [[video mapping]] technology, and events are sometimes held in the surrounding square on these occasions. Day]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dha.com.tr/istanbul/istanbulun-simgeleri-dunya-kanser-gununde-mavi-ve-turuncuya-burundu/haber-1624625|title=İstanbul'un simgeleri Dünya Kanser Günü'nde mavi ve == Cultural impact ==
[[File:Галатская башня в лунном свете.jpg|thumb|''Galata Tower in Moonlight'', [[Ivan Aivazovsky]] (1845)]] Certain works, particularly those in [[Turkish literature]], contain references to the tower and descriptions influenced by it. In the following [[couplet]], which means, "[O my beloved!] Your lovers are merely displaying flags to you; do not think that they have enlisted as daredevil soldiers like Rezmî," [[Rezmî]] alludes to the tower's function of signaling fires. Drawing on the motif of burning with love for the beloved, he explains that although other lovers wave flags to indicate that they are "burning" with passion, he himself has enlisted as a genuine lover in the ranks of the [[serdengeçti]] (literally, one who has surrendered his head, or a soldier willing to risk his life):<ref name="Tanrıbuyurdu">{{cite journal |url=http://www.dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/317457 |title=Klâsik Türk edebiyatına yansıyan yönleriyle "Galata" |first=Gülçin |last=Tanrıbuyurdu |journal=İnsan ve Toplum Bilimleri Araştırmaları Dergisi |volume=6 |issue=1 |year=2017 |pages=21-42|access-date=12 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206090905/http://www.itobiad.com/tr/download/article-file/317457 |archive-date=6 February 2021 |url-status=dead }}</ref> {{quote2|Do not think that your lovers display banners to you<br> Like warriors in battle, they have been inscribed as those who have surrendered their heads}}

The same situation is referenced in a couplet by [[Gelibolulu Mustafa Ali]]:<ref name="Tanrıbuyurdu"/> {{quote2|The sparks of my nocturnal sigh revealed a procession from the heights<br> How many banners unfurled, as flames blazed in glorious orange above}}

In the section concerning Galata Tower in [[Cemal Süreya]]'s poem "Burkulmuş Altın Hâli Güneşin" ("The Twisted Golden State of the Sun"), nostalgia for the Byzantine and Roman periods is expressed through [[irony]] employing the literary device of [[allusion]]:<ref>{{cite journal |title=Cemal Süreya şiirinde ironi |first=Muhammed |last=Hüküm |journal=Türklük Bilimi Araştırmaları |year=2017 |issue=42 |pages=77-107|doi=10.17133/tubar.365351}}</ref> {{quote2|And Galata Tower (its hat flew off in 1514, during Byzantine times, and it was circumcised by the Turks in 1967), having gathered the buildings around itself, is looking for ways to comfortably withstand an approaching storm, holding meetings: at the head of its people and in the foremost position, like Pharaoh preparing to knock on the gates of hell...}}

[[File:Hezarfen Ahmed Çelebi.jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.7|A 1950 [[Postage stamps and postal history of Turkey|Turkish postage stamp]] depicting [[Hezârfen Ahmed Çelebi]] gliding from Galata Tower, issued in commemoration of the [[International Civil Aviation Organization]] Congress that began on 17 October 1950]] The tower is also mentioned in Süreya's poem entitled "Rokoko".<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/73232 |title=İstanbul'a iki bakış: Sezai Karakoç ve Cemal Süreya'nın şiirlerinde İstanbul |first=M. Fatih |last=Andı |journal=İlmi Araştırmalar |year=1998 |issue=6 |pages=7-34|access-date=21 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522014605/https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/73232 |archive-date=22 May 2021 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In [[Sezai Karakoç]]'s poem "Kızkulesi'ne Gazel II", the poet describes the [[Maiden's Tower]] as a Muslim structure and Galata Tower as a Christian one. He states that the Maiden's Tower sends light to Galata Tower, dispelling the Genoese and Byzantine darkness surrounding it. Interpreting the former tower as a symbol of the [[Eastern world|East]] and the latter as a symbol of [[Western world|Western civilization]], the poem suggests that the mystery and enchantment of the East will also influence the West:<ref>{{cite journal |title=Sezai Karakoç'un şiirlerinde medeniyet şehri İstanbul'un tarihî ve manevi unsurları |journal=Turkish Studies: International Periodical For the Languages, Literature and History of Turkish or Turkic |first=Fikri |last=Kula |first2=Mehmet |last2=Güneş |year=2016 |volume=11 |issue=10 |pages=397-422|doi=10.7827/TurkishStudies.9693}}</ref> {{quote2|The Maiden's Tower sends light to Galata Tower<br>It dispels the Genoese darkness<br>The Byzantine darkness every morning<br>With the Muslim lullaby it hears in the waters every evening<br>It engraves the spellbinding language into the depths of our souls<br>It spreads into the air an evening scented with walnut leaves from Samarkand<br>It is a green prayer for the greatest illumination}}

[[Ümit Yaşar Oğuzcan]] wrote the poem "Galata Kulesi" ("Galata Tower") following the death of his 15-year-old son Vedat, who died by suicide after jumping from the tower on 6 June 1973.<ref>{{web citation|url=https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/603874|title=Ümit Yaşar Oğuzcan'ın şiir dünyası|first=Abide|last=Doğan|journal=Hacettepe Üniversitesi Edebiyat Fakültesi Dergisi|year=2003|volume=20|issue=1|pages=71-84|access-date=22 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522014537/https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/603874|archive-date=22 May 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his book ''[[Constantinople (De Amicis book)|Constantinople]]'', published in 1877, [[Edmondo De Amicis]] likened Galata to an "open fan" and the tower perched atop the hill to "the handle of this fan".<ref name="Tanrıbuyurdu"/>

In the 2011 video game ''[[Assassin's Creed: Revelations]]'', which is set partly in 16th-century Constantinople, the protagonist [[Ezio Auditore da Firenze]] climbs the exterior of Galata Tower and enters it during one section of the game. Galata Tower is also among the Great Buildings featured in the 2012 browser game ''[[Forge of Empires]]''. The 1997 video game ''[[Byzantine (video game)|Byzantine: The Betrayal]]'' includes sections set in Galata Tower.<ref>{{web citation|url=http://www.gameboomers.com/wtcheats/pcBb/ByzantineDan.htm|title=Byzantine: The Betrayal|publisher=GameBoomers|language=English|first=Dan|last=Kennedy|date=July 2002|access-date=20 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170420231446/http://www.gameboomers.com/wtcheats/pcBb/ByzantineDan.htm|archive-date=20 April 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{web citation|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/en-iyi-10-yerli-bilgisayar-oyunu-10303112|title=En iyi 10 yerli bilgisayar oyunu|date=7 November 2008|work=Hürriyet|access-date=20 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200204090504/http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/en-iyi-10-yerli-bilgisayar-oyunu-10303112|archive-date=4 February 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> A depiction of the tower appears on the Galata map in the 2017 video game ''[[Sabotaj (video game)|Sabotaj]]''.<ref>{{web citation|url=https://www.gamerozzi.com/sabotaj-steame-geliyor/|title=Sabotaj Steam'e geliyor!|publisher=Gamerozzi|first=Abide Sevde|last=Alioğlu Yıldırak|date=20 November 2020|access-date=20 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522014605/https://www.gamerozzi.com/sabotaj-steame-geliyor/|archive-date=22 May 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Galata Tower is depicted in two paintings by [[Ivan Aivazovsky]] dating from 1845 and 1846, each showing a different view of the city. Galata and the tower are depicted in a painting by [[Garabet Yazmaciyan]] dated 1891,<ref>{{web citation|url=https://www.istanbulsanatevi.com/sanatcilar/soyadi-y/yazmaciyan-garabet/garabet-yazmaciyan-galata-kulesi-6546/|title=Garabet Yazmacıyan Galata Kulesi|publisher=İstanbul Sanat Evi|access-date=22 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107014651/https://www.istanbulsanatevi.com/sanatcilar/soyadi-y/yazmaciyan-garabet/garabet-yazmaciyan-galata-kulesi-6546/|archive-date=7 January 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> while his 1903 painting portrays a fire that broke out near the tower.<ref>{{web citation|url=https://www.istanbulsanatevi.com/sanatcilar/soyadi-y/yazmaciyan-garabet/garabet-yazmaciyan-galata-yangini-6552/|title=Garabet Yazmacıyan Galata Yangını|publisher=İstanbul Sanat Evi|access-date=22 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522073353/https://www.istanbulsanatevi.com/sanatcilar/soyadi-y/yazmaciyan-garabet/garabet-yazmaciyan-galata-yangini-6552/|archive-date=22 May 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[İbrahim Safi]] also produced two paintings depicting the tower.<ref>{{web citation|url=https://www.istanbulsanatevi.com/sanatcilar/soyadi-s/safi-ibrahim/ibrahim-safi-galata-kulesi-6441/|title=İbrahim Safi Galata Kulesi|publisher=İstanbul Sanat Evi|access-date=22 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201029051315/https://www.istanbulsanatevi.com/sanatcilar/soyadi-s/safi-ibrahim/ibrahim-safi-galata-kulesi-6441/|archive-date=29 October 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{web citation|url=https://www.istanbulsanatevi.com/sanatcilar/soyadi-s/safi-ibrahim/ibrahim-safi-galata-kulesi-sokagi-9875/|title=İbrahim Safi Galata Kulesi Sokağı|publisher=İstanbul Sanat Evi|access-date=22 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522073341/https://www.istanbulsanatevi.com/sanatcilar/soyadi-s/safi-ibrahim/ibrahim-safi-galata-kulesi-sokagi-9875/|archive-date=22 May 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref> Various depictions of the tower also appear in books by numerous writers describing their visits to the city.<ref name="Sağlam"/>

[[File:Koenigs Wusterhausen Niederlehme Wasserturm.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|The water tower in [[Niederlehme]], designed after Galata Tower]] The logos of the Beyoğlu Municipality<ref>{{web citation|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/beyoglu-belediyesinden-logo-aciklamasi-41447676|title=Beyoğlu Belediyesi'nden 'logo' açıklaması|work=Hürriyet|publisher=[[Demirören News Agency]]|date=14 February 2020|location=Istanbul|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210107184124/https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/beyoglu-belediyesinden-logo-aciklamasi-41447676|archive-date=7 January 2021|access-date=6 January 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref> and [[Istanbul Galata University]]<ref>{{web citation|url=https://docplayer.biz.tr/199053520-1-01-galata-universitesi-logotype-ina-dair-temel-oranlar-asagida-belirtilmistir-oranlar-kesinlikle-degistirilmemelidir.html|title=Temel unsurlar|publisher=[[Istanbul Galata University]]|page=1|access-date=22 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220726080048/https://docplayer.biz.tr/199053520-1-01-galata-universitesi-logotype-ina-dair-temel-oranlar-asagida-belirtilmistir-oranlar-kesinlikle-degistirilmemelidir.html|archive-date=26 July 2022|url-status=dead}}</ref> feature depictions of the tower. Among the models displayed at [[Miniatürk]] in the district since the park opened in May 2003 is a model of Galata Tower.<ref>{{web 2016.<ref>{{web citation|url=https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/kultur-sanat/miniaturkteki-5-maket-yenilendi/545573|title=Miniatürk'teki 5 maket yenilendi|first=Sefa|last=Mutlu|date=29 March 2016|location=Istanbul|publisher=Anadolu Agency|access-date=20 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210520060920/https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/kultur-sanat/miniaturkteki-5-maket-yenilendi/545573|archive-date=20 May 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref> A model of the tower is also exhibited at [[Minimundus]] in the Austrian city of [[Klagenfurt]].<ref>{{web citation|url=https://www.minimundus.at/en/objekt/galata-tower-istanbul/|title=Galata Tower, Istanbul|publisher=[[Minimundus]] official website|language=English|access-date=20 May those exhibited at the [[Kepez Open-Air Museum]], which opened in [[Konyaaltı]], [[Antalya]], in May 2004 and moved to [[Kepez, Antalya|Kepez]] in 2018.<ref>{{web citation|url=https://v3.arkitera.com/v1/haberler/2004/05/31/minicity.htm|title=Mini City sahipsiz kaldı|publisher=Arkitera|date=31 May 2004|first=Hakkı|last=Sargın|work=Akşam|access-date=20 May Among the sand sculptures exhibited at the International Sand Sculpture Festival held at the [[CarrefourSA]] branch in [[Kozyatağı]] between July and September 2007 was a sculpture themed around Galata Tower and [[Hezârfen Ahmed Çelebi]].<ref>{{web citation|url=http://arsiv.sabah.com.tr/2007/06/30/gny/haber,571AEDC643504FE4BF33FD45291D3AE9.html|title=Kum heykeller İstanbul'da|work=Sabah The [[water tower]] in the town of [[Niederlehme]], in the German state of [[Brandenburg]], completed in 1902, was designed after Galata Tower.<ref>{{book citation |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5L26xEfvJiIC&q=%22Niederlehme%22+%22galata%22&dq=%22Niederlehme%22+%22galata%22&hl=tr&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwj29uHR7tfwAhUCS60KHejrDh0Q6AEwAnoECAMQAg |title=Brandenburg |volume=18 |first=Georg |last=Dehio |editor1-first=Gerhard |editor1-last=Vinken |editor2-first=Barbara |editor2-last=Rimpel |page=12 |language=German |publisher=Deutscher Kunstverlag |year=2012 |isbn=3422031235 |access-date=20 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210520090424/https://books.google.com/books?id=5L26xEfvJiIC&q=%22Niederlehme%22+%22galata%22&dq=%22Niederlehme%22+%22galata%22&hl=tr&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwj29uHR7tfwAhUCS60KHejrDh0Q6AEwAnoECAMQAg |archive-date=20 May 2021 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Indooroopilly State High School Buildings''' is a heritage-listed collection of buildings at [[Indooroopilly State High School]] at Ward Street, [[Indooroopilly, Queensland|Indooroopilly]], [[City of Brisbane]], [[Queensland]], Australia. It was designed by [[Boulton & Paul Ltd]], [[Department of Public Works (Queensland)]] and built from 1953 to 1963. It was added to the [[Queensland Heritage Register]] on 14 October 2016.<ref name=qhr>{{cite QHR||Indooroopilly State High School|650035|accessdate=15 February 2018}}</ref>

== History ==
Indooroopilly State High School (SHS) opened in early 1954 in response to post-[[World War II]] (WWII) population growth in [[Brisbane]]'s suburbs and the growing demand for secondary education. As of 2025, Indooroopilly SHS retains its original complex of seven timber and brick buildings constructed during 1953–59:
* A Block (1953–54)
* B Block  (1954)
* C Block  (1954–55)
* Building A6 (1955)
* D Block  (1957–58)
* E Block  (1958–59)
* G Block  (1958–59)
These buildings are constructed from a range of standard materials and structural methods employed by the [[Department of Public Works (Queensland)|Department of Public Works]] (DPW) during the 1950s, including: prefabricated Boulton & Paul timber units (blocks A and B); timber trusses (blocks A and C); and steel open-web trusses (blocks D and E). The buildings also feature differences in roof form, glazing, and [[verandah]] and stair arrangements that illustrate changes to standard school building types throughout the late-1950s. The school retains its organic 1950s site planning of long classroom blocks positioned in response to existing and man-made contours, spiralling around a high point in the centre of the steeply-sloping site. Blocks are connected by covered areas and walkways, and landscape elements include brick planter boxes, concrete stairs and pavements, a bitumen parade ground and roadways, retaining walls, gardens, mature trees, and sporting facilities such as a {{circa|1959}} oval and mid-1960s basketball and tennis courts. The school has been in continuous operation since its establishment.<ref name="qhr" />

The suburb of Indooroopilly is located {{convert|7|km}} southwest of the [[Brisbane CBD]]. Although the Indooroopilly area was surveyed as farm allotments in 1858, central Indooroopilly did not attract agricultural settlement to the same extent as nearby [[Fig Tree Pocket, Queensland|Fig Tree Pocket]], [[St Lucia, Queensland|St Lucia]] and [[Long Pocket, Queensland|Long Pocket]]; and its development was limited until the [[Main Line railway, Queensland|Brisbane to Ipswich railway line]] opened to the locality in 1875. In the late 19th century a small township developed near the [[Indooroopilly railway station]], and a number of large villas were erected on the banks of the [[Brisbane River]]. By the 1920s further subdivision had created a busy suburb, and growth was also facilitated by the opening of the [[Walter Taylor Bridge|Walter Taylor Road Bridge]])in 1936.<ref name="qhr-1">DNRM Survey Plan S151857, 1858</ref><ref>'Combined Services Detailed Interrogation Centre (former)' QHR 650030</ref><ref>'Tighnabruaich', QHR 600229</ref><ref>Allom Lovell and Associates Pty Ltd, "Tighnabruaich: a historical survey and management plan", for the Department of Housing and Construction Brisbane April 1985, pp.6-12</ref><ref>'Brisbane Heritage Trails, Eye on Indooroopilly' Brochure,&nbsp;</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/things-to-see-and-do/outdoor-activities/walking/walking-trails/heritage-trails/indooroopilly-heritage-trail|title=Eye on Indooroopilly Heritage Trail|last=|first=|date=|website=[[Brisbane City Council]]|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200411025301/https://www.brisbane.qld.gov.au/things-to-see-and-do/outdoor-activities/walking/walking-trails/heritage-trails/indooroopilly-heritage-trail|archive-date=11 April 2020|access-date=2020-04-11}}</ref> Indooroopilly's population (including [[Taringa, Queensland|Taringa]]) rose from 1029 in 1911, to 2048 in 1921, and 8565 by 1947.<ref name="qhr-2">'Indooroopilly', http://queenslandplaces.com.au/indooroopilly {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210626020459/https://queenslandplaces.com.au/indooroopilly |date=26 June 2021 }} (accessed 28.7.2016).</ref><ref name="qhr" />

Early schools near Indooroopilly included Toowong Mixed School (opened 1870, now [[Ironside State School]], St Lucia) and Indooroopilly State School, opened in 1889.<ref name="qhr-3">Queensland State Archives Agency ID5341, Ironside State School</ref><ref>Queensland State Archives Agency ID5328, Indooroopilly State School. The Toowong school's building was opened in 1871 ('An Introduction to the History of St Lucia', St Lucia History Group, July 2006, p.7). It was later called Indooroopilly State School, then Indooroopilly Pocket State School, and finally Ironside State School from 1905.</ref> The establishment of schools was considered an essential step in the development of early communities and integral to their success. The State Education Act 1875 provided for free, compulsory and secular primary education and established the [[Department of Public Instruction (Queensland)|Department of Public Instruction]]. Schools became a community focus, a symbol of progress, and a source of pride, with enduring connections formed with past pupils, parents, and teachers.<ref name="qhr-4">Project Services, "Mount Morgan State High School" in Queensland Schools Heritage Study Part II Report, for Education Queensland, 2008, pp.4-5</ref><ref>Paul Burmester, Margaret Pullar and Michael Kennedy, Queensland Schools: A Heritage Conservation Study, a report for the Department of Education, 1996, pp.91-2</ref><ref>Thom Blake, "Educating Queenslanders" in Queensland Historical Thematic Framework, 2007 (rev. 2013 by EHP), p. 2</ref><ref>Greg Logan and Eddie Clarke, State Education in Queensland: a brief history, a report for the Department of Education, Queensland, 1984, p. 2.</ref><ref name="qhr" />

After WWII, Indooroopilly was chosen as the site for a new state high school. In Queensland, governments were slow to establish state secondary education, considering it to be of little relevance to Queensland's primary industry-based economy. It was not until 1912 that the government instituted a high school system, whereby separate high schools were established in major towns or, where the student population was too small, a primary school was expanded to include a "high top". In Queensland generally, high schools remained few in number until after WWII, when secondary education was generally accepted as essential and was more widely provided for.<ref name=qhr-5>Blake, "Educating Queenslanders" in Queensland Historical Thematic Framework, pp.9-11</ref><ref>Burmester et al, Queensland Schools: A Heritage Conservation Study, pp.32-35.</ref><ref name=qhr/>

In 1954 it was reported that high school enrolments in Queensland had more than doubled since 1948, from 4500 to nearly 11,000.<ref name=qhr-6>'Big expansion is planned. New high school buildings now on priority list', Sunday Mail, 14 November 1954, p.7.</ref> The Department of Public Instruction was largely unprepared for the enormous demand for state education that began in the late 1940s and continued well into the 1960s. This was a nationwide occurrence resulting from immigration and the unprecedented population growth now termed the "[[baby boom]]".<ref name=qhr-7>Project Services, Queensland Schools Heritage Study Part II Report, for Education Queensland, January 2008, pp.28-31.</ref> Queensland schools were faced with enormous overcrowding and a lack of resources because the [[Government of Queensland|Queensland Government]] and community saw education as a low priority and provided the department with only a small budget. The overriding concern for the Department of Public Instruction was the need to build school buildings as expeditiously and economically as possible.<ref name=qhr-8>Burmester et al, Queensland Schools A Heritage Conservation Study, p. 70.</ref><ref name=qhr/>

The Queensland Government had a long-standing practice of developing standard plans for its school buildings, which helped ensure consistency and economy throughout the state. From the 1860s until the 1960s, Queensland school buildings were predominantly timber-framed, and standard designs were continually refined in response to changing needs and educational philosophy. Queensland school buildings were particularly innovative in climate control, lighting, and ventilation.<ref name=qhr-9>Burmester et al, Queensland Schools: A Heritage Conservation Study, pp.84, 120-1.</ref> In the post-WWII period, the pressures of material shortages and rapid population growth forced the DPW to experiment with prefabrication and new, more efficient structural systems in order to keep up with demand for additional school buildings.<ref name=qhr-10>Burmester et al, Queensland Schools: A Heritage Conservation Study, pp. 70-82.</ref><ref name=qhr/>

In an attempt to relieve the pressure on the existing state high schools in central Brisbane,<ref name=qhr-11>The Industrial State High School, the Commercial State High School, the Domestic Science State High School, and Brisbane State High School. In early 1954 it was reported that the three new schools had relieved the pressure on South Brisbane SHS and the Commercial SHS ('Schools taking 15,000', Brisbane Telegraph, 2 February 1954, p.4).</ref> which did not have sufficient room to expand, a decision was made in 1950 to establish three new suburban high schools, which would commence with an initial intake of Year 9 pupils and grow over four years.<ref name=qhr-12>Rod Bailey, Palma Jubilee, Indooroopilly State High School 1954-2004, Indooroopilly SHS 2004, pp.9, 78.</ref> Reflecting the growth of suburbanisation and a move towards a decentralised population in urban centres, new high schools were located in suburban areas rather than the centre of town. This allowed for large grounds with ample room for sports facilities. The general classroom buildings were the same standard types as used for primary schools but high schools also included purpose-built facilities such as science laboratories, domestic science buildings, workshops for woodwork and metal work, libraries, and gymnasiums. These were also built to standard plans but were specific to their use and not a continuation of previous designs.<ref name=qhr-13>Burmester et al, Queensland Schools: A Heritage Conservation Study, p.75.</ref><ref name=qhr/>

There was also a focus on the fit between the school and its neighbourhood, as well as site planning for expansion. In the early 1950s, architects developed master planning concepts that influenced the design and layout of the whole school.
